topicName: Rack Middleware Stack and Custom Middleware
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding the Rack Middleware Stack in Ruby on Rails"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"At the core of Ruby on Rails lies Rack, a modular and lightweight interface for developing web applications in Ruby. Rack applications are wrapped in a stack of middleware components that process HTTP requests before they reach your application controller and handle responses on their way back to the client."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"How the Rack Pipeline Works"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Every HTTP request entering a Rails application flows through a sequence of middleware classes. Each middleware component can inspect, modify, or halt the request, pass it down to the next middleware in the stack, and finally process the resulting response."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Requests move top-down through the middleware stack."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Responses move bottom-up back through the stack."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Common built-in middleware includes ActionDispatch::Session, Rack::Cors, and Rack::Runtime."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Inspecting Your Application Middleware Stack"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can inspect the current order and composition of your Rails middleware stack by running a simple terminal command within your application directory:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"bin/rails middleware"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Building a Custom Rack Middleware"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"A valid Rack middleware must meet two simple requirements: it needs to implement an initialize method accepting the downstream application (app), and a call method accepting an env hash representing the HTTP request."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"class RequestTimer
  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    start_time = Time.now
    status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
    duration = (Time.now - start_time) * 1000
    headers['X-Response-Time'] = "#{duration.round(2)}ms"
    [status, headers, body]
  end
end"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Registering Middleware in Rails"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once you have created your custom middleware class, you must configure Rails to include it in the middleware stack. This is typically done inside the config/application.rb file or environment-specific configuration files."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"module MyApp
  class Application < Rails::Application
    config.load_defaults 7.0
    
    # Insert custom middleware before a specific middleware
    config.middleware.use RequestTimer
  end
end"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Middleware Insertion Methods"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Rails provides flexible methods to position your middleware precisely where you need it within the request lifecycle execution pipeline."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"config.middleware.use(new_middleware) adds the middleware to the bottom of the stack."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"config.middleware.insert_before(ExistingMiddleware, new_middleware) inserts the new middleware before the specified class."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"config.middleware.insert_after(ExistingMiddleware, new_middleware) places the new middleware immediately after the specified class."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering Rack middleware empowers you to intercept requests globally, implement cross-cutting concerns like logging, security headers, rate limiting, and performance tracking cleanly outside of your Rails controllers."}]
